A plan becomes reliable when each requirement has a **source**, an **applicability**, a **status**, and a **linked Issue**. This page lists the requirements of the fictional thesis in that form. It is the worked example for exercise [X2](../course/exercises/x2.qmd).

## Rules versus plans

Three kinds of statements appear in a thesis plan, and they have different authority.

1. **Course rules** govern this workshop. They come from the KSL entry of the course. They say nothing about your thesis.
2. **Thesis rules** govern the master's thesis in one study programme. They come from the study plan of that programme and from the faculty regulations. They differ between programmes.
3. **Plans and practices** are decisions that you take, for example a data management plan, a rule for AI use, or the date of a milestone. They are context-dependent tasks, **not** universal exam rules.

The fictional student studies the **MA Digital Humanities as a Major**. The rules below apply to that programme only. A student who takes DH as a **Minor** or as an elective writes the thesis in another programme and must use the rules of that programme.

## Thesis rules for the DH Major

Status values: **verified** means that the text was checked in the cited document on the retrieval date. **unconfirmed** means that the rule exists, but a detail (usually a date) is not in the cited source. **fictional** means that the workshop replaces a real value with an invented one.

## Unresolved

- **Real dates.** No real registration or submission date is in the cited sources. The workshop uses the fictional dates 2026-12-01 and 2027-06-01. A real student asks the Dean's Office.
- **Which study plan applies.** SP-DH-2025 Art. 26 (p. 7) says that students who start Digital Humanities from spring semester 2025 fall under this plan, and that Minor students under the plan of 9 November 2020 transfer to it. The cited text does not state the case of Major students who started earlier. Such a student checks with the programme.
- **A cross-reference.** SP-DH-2025 Art. 16 Abs. 1 refers to "the written work according to Article 16"; the written thesis is regulated in Article 15. The register reads it as a reference to Article 15. Confirm with the programme if it matters.
- **Format.** The cited sources set length and language, but no citation style, layout, or number of copies. Those come from the supervisor or the Dean's Office.
:::

## Course rules (KSL)

These facts govern the workshop, not the thesis. They come from the [KSL course entry](https://www.ksl.unibe.ch/KSL/kurzansicht?stammNr=526141&semester=HS2026&lfdNr=0). See the [syllabus](../course/syllabus.qmd).

| --- | --- |

| Type of exam: not defined | KSL |
| Pass rule: attend the full session and show the minimum deliverable | Instructor ([syllabus](../course/syllabus.qmd#assessment)) |
| Room: Seminarraum F 001, Hörraumgebäude Unitobler | KSL |

## Context-dependent tasks

These tasks appear in the plan because good practice or a third party may require them. They are **not** exam rules of the DH Major. Each one needs its own source when it applies.

| Task | When it applies | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data management plan | A funder, a project, or the institute requires it. | E02-T2 |
| Ethics review | The research involves people or sensitive data. | E02-T3 |
| Rules for AI use | Always agree them with the supervisor; university guidelines may apply. | E02-T4 |
| Rights and access decision | Before anything is published. | E08-T2 |
| Release and deposit | Only after the rights decision. | E08-T3, E08-T5 |
